title: Cheese, Leek and Potato Pie
subtitle: A vegetarian shortcrust pie with cheddar and soft leeks
excerpt: Tender potato, sweet leeks and sharp cheddar in a creamy filling, encased in golden shortcrust pastry. A filling vegetarian supper that works hot or cold.
sourceNotes: British home-baking tradition, developed for a standard 23cm pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C until hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a day ahead and keep chilled. Assemble and bake when ready.

content.text: This vegetarian pie is held together by a creamy cheddar sauce with soft leeks and chunks of potato. Cook the potatoes until just tender, not mushy. The filling must be cold before it goes into the pastry or the base will go soft.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Boil the potato chunks in salted water for 10 minutes until just tender. Drain well and leave to steam dry.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the leeks and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk slowly, stirring all the time. Cook until the sauce thickens. Stir in the cheddar and mustard. Season well with salt and pepper.
Fold the potato chunks through the sauce gently. Spread onto a tray and leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish, leaving a little overhang.
Spoon the cold filling into the case. Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg, press the lid on, and crimp the edges firmly.
Cut a small slit in the top. Brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The base is soft and undercooked.
items.cause: The filling was warm when it went in, or the oven was too cool.
items.fix: Cool the filling fully first. Bake the pie on a preheated baking sheet placed low in the oven.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: The milk was added too quickly and the roux did not thicken properly.
items.fix: Add the milk a splash at a time, stirring constantly, and let the sauce bubble for 2 minutes before taking it off the heat.

items.symptom: The potato breaks apart in the filling.
items.cause: The potatoes were overcooked before mixing.
items.fix: Boil the chunks until just tender, then drain and cool before folding them in gently.
